parent_prompt:
You receive 7 images. Image 1 is the LAYOUT SKETCH of the finished 1920x1080 game screen: a crude flat-colour blocking that fixes the exact composition - camera, horizon, wall and floor lines, and the position, size and outline of every object. Repaint image 1 into a finished painting: keep every line and every block exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is, paint each block as the object described below, do not move, enlarge, shrink, add or remove anything, and leave no flat colour areas or hard geometric edges. Images 2-6 are photos of the real place (geography, architecture, materials and real details to paint from; they are references only, do not copy their camera, cars, people, signs or weather). Image 7 is a finished background painting from our game: use it ONLY as the reference for the painting technique (brushwork, palette, edge softness, level of detail, line quality); do not copy anything from its scene.

Place: the OLD Stary most in Bratislava as it was in 1995 - the long riveted steel truss bridge over the Danube between Petrzalka and the Old Town (rebuilt after 1945, demolished in 2013). We stand on its upstream wooden footway above the first river pier near the Petrzalka end and look upstream across the Danube. Image 2 is a photo taken from this bridge in exactly this direction: the castle hill with Bratislava castle, the slender spire of St Martin's cathedral and the Old Town riverfront. Image 3 is this very footway: weathered wooden planks laid across it, a plain grey steel railing with thin vertical bars on the river side, the riveted grey truss on the other side. Image 4 shows the riveted grey truss members with their gusset plates full of rivet heads. Image 5 is Most SNP in 1988: the bridge deck hung from one slanted pylon carrying the round saucer restaurant. Image 6 shows the castle in 1991, before its later renovation: warm ochre-yellow walls, dark slate-grey roofs and dark pointed caps on the four corner towers - paint the castle with these 1990s colours, not white with red roofs. Paint 1995: no glass office towers, no modern riverside buildings of the 2000s and 2010s, no big river-cruise hotel ships, no cranes, no billboards.

Brief: an invented small service booth of the bridge maintenance stands on the footway; it holds an isolated demo circuit, three mechanical number wheels and a stand for a measuring coil; next to it a small table for a metronome; the Danube below the railing. Thursday 15 June 1995, a sunny early-summer afternoon: warm sunlight from the upper left, the river sparkling, a blue sky with a few white clouds.

Camera: standing on the bridge, about 2.4 m above the footway planks, looking straight out across the footway and its railing; the railing runs parallel to the picture; vertical lines stay vertical; horizon at y ~400. We are high above the water, so the river lies below us and the far banks are low in the picture. Keep this exact geometry from the sketch: the far waterline of the Old Town bank at y ~410; the Petrzalka bank on the left coming nearer towards the left edge (its waterline at y ~505 at the left edge); the railing standing on y 800 with its top rail at y 617; the footway planks from y 800 down to the bottom edge; the booth roof at y 335-372.

What the sketch blocks are, left to right: at the very left and right edges two big riveted grey inclined steel members of the bridge truss (the near truss we stand beside), rising out of the top of the picture and framing it, full of rivet heads; on the left the small invented service booth standing on a little bay of the footway: faded grey-green painted sheet metal, a sloping corrugated roof with a short mast and a small plain red pennant, a wide open front hatch whose flap is propped up as an awning, a wooden counter shelf in the hatch carrying the props; the dense green park trees of the Petrzalka bank behind the booth with its low stone embankment; Most SNP left of centre: the slanted grey pylon leaning to the left with the round saucer restaurant on top, its stay cables fanning down to the thin bridge deck that crosses the river to the foot of the castle hill; hazy green hills far upstream; in the centre the green castle hill with fortification walls and the castle on top; the cathedral with its slender green-copper spire to the right of the castle hill; the Old Town riverfront to the right: old houses and palaces with red tiled roofs, a white 1950s hotel block, a long baroque barracks building with a rust-red modern gallery wing on top of it, a row of trees along the stone embankment; the white riverboat moored at the passenger quay; the wide blue-green Danube with sun glitter on the left; the grey steel footway railing with posts and thin vertical bars; the small round metronome table at the railing right of the booth; the wooden plank footway.

Interactive props - each painted clearly inside its block, the same size as its block, easy to recognise at a glance:
1. the block of the layout sketch at x 170-295, y 488-623 of the 1920x1080 frame (9-15 % from the left, 45-58 % from the top): an empty round steel holder ring with a small keyed notch, mounted upright on a short post at the left end of the booth counter (no coil in it yet).
2. the block of the layout sketch at x 418-558, y 535-627 of the 1920x1080 frame (22-29 % from the left, 50-58 % from the top): a grey steel box with three big mechanical number wheels side by side, each showing 0, at the right end of the booth counter.
3. the block of the layout sketch at x 622-788, y 640-800 of the 1920x1080 frame (32-41 % from the left, 59-74 % from the top): a small round wooden table on one leg with a painted white circle mark on its top, standing at the railing (empty - no metronome on it yet).
4. the block of the layout sketch at x 1240-1560, y 400-466 of the 1920x1080 frame (65-81 % from the left, 37-43 % from the top): a white Danube passenger riverboat of the 1990s with a red funnel stripe, moored at the Old Town quay across the river (no name, no lettering).
5. the block of the layout sketch at x 860-1160, y 615-800 of the 1920x1080 frame (45-60 % from the left, 57-74 % from the top): a stretch of the grey steel footway railing with the Danube far below it.
Between the coil ring and the number wheels the counter carries the isolated demo circuit: a wooden board with insulated red and blue wires, terminals and a small lamp. The footway continues out of the left edge behind the left truss member (the area of the layout sketch at x 0-90, y 800-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (0-5 % from the left, 74-94 % from the top)).

Walkable floor: the band at x 18-1902, y 815-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (1-99 % from the left, 75-94 % from the top) is the footway of weathered wooden planks - one continuous flat surface with no kerb, no step, no edge inside it, and nothing standing on it: no benches, no bins, no bicycles, no lamp posts. Only sunlight, soft shadows, the plank joints and a few worn spots.
This room has no NPC zones.

Fiction rules: the service booth, the demo circuit, the number wheels, the coil holder and the table are fictional props; no signs or lettering on the booth, no traffic signs, no boat names, no brands, no flags with emblems, no people, no animals. The only digits in the picture are the three zeros on the number wheels.

The layout sketch is a blocking aid only: paint over all of it. Do NOT draw frames, borders, outlines or boxes around objects, and keep no flat colour block. The finished picture contains no UI, no captions, no text except what is asked for above, no watermark and no people or animals unless stated above.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
